description: REQ-305's own Edge Case text (specs/behavioral-spec.md, 'The ledger write ("active") succeeds but the SUBSEQUENT registry-append write fails FOR A TRANSIENT REASON (e.g. a filesystem error): THE SYSTEM SHALL retry the registry-append on the NEXT wake before any further spawn evaluation runs -- a child marked "active" in the ledger but absent from the registry is a detectable inconsistency ... never a silent, permanent gap') is not implemented anywhere in the delivered code, and this is the NEW orchestrator wiring this sprint itself wrote (not reused-unmodified sprint-1 code). In executeSpawnAttempt's step 9 (spawn-orchestrator.mjs), the ledger 'active' row write (line 685) is followed by an UNGUARDED `await appendCitizenRecord(citizensRegistryFile, citizenRecord)` call (line 697) with zero try/catch -- only the SEPARATE isSelfFunded()===false rejection path (lines 696-701) is explicitly handled. A genuinely transient filesystem error thrown by appendCitizenRecord (ENOTDIR/EACCES/ENOSPC/etc, unrelated to isSelfFunded) propagates as an UNCAUGHT PROMISE REJECTION out of executeSpawnAttempt, violating its own documented return-type contract (JSDoc line 463: `@returns {Promise<{status: "active"|"failed", childId: string|null, error?: string}>}` -- a rejection is neither of these two resolved shapes). I independently reproduced this: pointing citizensRegistryFile at a path whose parent segment is a plain file (not a directory) causes appendCitizenRecord's own fsp.mkdir(dirname,{recursive:true}) to throw ENOTDIR; executeSpawnAttempt's returned promise REJECTS with that raw error, even though the ledger's 'active' row for that child_id was already correctly, honestly written moments earlier (confirmed by reading children.jsonl after the rejection: the 'active' row IS present). No retry-on-next-wake mechanism exists anywhere in the codebase (grep across skills/self/spawn for 'transient'/'retry' returns zero matches related to this edge case) -- the affected child would be marked 'active' in the ledger FOREVER but PERMANENTLY absent from citizens.json, silently excluded from REQ-101's colony-surplus aggregation on every future wake with no code path that ever revisits it, directly contradicting the spec's own 'never a silent, permanent gap' promise. This is a genuine hole in the verification architecture's own coverage, not merely an implementation slip some other tracked obligation would have caught: no PROP anywhere in verification-architecture.md names this edge case (confirmed by grep for 'transient'/'retry.*next wake' -- zero matches), so it was never going to surface via the standard CRIT-205 '31 targeted obligations' gate either. No test in the delivered suite exercises this path: spawn-orchestrator.test.mjs's own 'PROP-307c step 9' test (line 287) breaks the FIRST write (the ledger append itself, via a blocked ledgerFile path) and its assertion is deliberately permissive of either a throw or a resolve, never actually reading ledger-file content to confirm what happened; the 'REQ-305 call-site: a successful attempt appends a citizens.json record' test (line 347) only covers the happy path. Note: withGigLock's own try/finally (economy/gig/lib/lock.mjs) does correctly release the 'colony-spawn' lock even when runAttempt throws here, so this is NOT a deadlock/lock-starvation risk and NOT a money-safety risk (no funds are at stake in this path) -- it is a bookkeeping/observability gap: a legitimately-active, self-funded child citizen can be permanently and silently dropped from colony accounting after a single rare filesystem hiccup, with the wake-cycle CLI (wake-gate.mjs)'s own top-level .catch() reporting only a generic 'wake-gate: fatal: <error>' with no indication that a child was in fact successfully activated.

evidence.snippet: appendChild(ledgerFile, { ...spec, status: "active", attempted_ms: nowMs, active_since: nowMs }); const citizenRecord = {...}; if (isSelfFunded(citizenRecord)) { await appendCitizenRecord(citizensRegistryFile, citizenRecord); } else { console.error(...); }  -- appendCitizenRecord itself (lines 107-117) is never wrapped in try/catch by its caller.
evidence.testName: Empirically reproduced fresh (not accepted from any prior evidence): a standalone script (identical happyDeps fixture from spawn-orchestrator.test.mjs, citizensRegistryFile pointed at <file>/citizens.json where <file> is a plain file, not a directory) drives executeSpawnAttempt to REJECT with 'ENOTDIR: not a directory, open .../citizens.json', while children.jsonl independently confirms the SAME attempt's ledger row was written with status:"active". No existing test (spawn-orchestrator.test.mjs's 'PROP-307c step 9' test at line 287, or the 'REQ-305 call-site' registry-append test at line 347) exercises this specific transient-registry-append-failure path; grep of specs/verification-architecture.md for 'transient'/'retry.*next wake' returns zero matches, confirming no PROP tracks this REQ-305 edge case at all.
